podcast.title: Influence on Other Musicians
podcast.body: Red Cross is noted as being very important to the musical education of musicians like Eddie Vedder and Dave Grohl. "Talk to Eddie Vetter or Dave Grohl, and they'll tell you how some of these bands were really, really important to their musical education."

xref.title: Red Cross Donation and Move to England (1990)
xref.body: Following the negative backlash and accusations of "ungratefulness" for boycotting awards, Sinead donated her house in Hollywood to the Red Cross. This enabled a family of refugees from Somalia to live there, and she subsequently moved back to England. "She was so appalled at the way she was treated for this so-called ungratefulness that she gave her Hollywood house to the Red Cross."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Enema of the State Cover Art Censorship
xref.body: The "Enema of the State" album cover underwent three different versions due to regulatory issues. The initial version featured a red cross on Lindemueller's hat and a capitalized 'B' in "Blink." The 'B' was corrected to lowercase, and subsequently, the American Red Cross intervened, citing the use of their symbol as a violation of the Geneva Convention, leading to its complete removal in the third and final version of the cover. "The American red cross saw the album and said using the red cross symbol in any other way than to signify the world of the real red cross is a violation of the Geneva convention."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Multiple Versions of "Enema of the State" Cover
xref.body: Blink-182's "Enema of the State" album had four different cover versions due to various issues and complaints. The initial version featured a Red Cross on Jeanine Lindemulder's hat and a capital "B" for the band's logo, which was corrected to a lowercase "b" in the second version. Following a complaint from the American Red Cross regarding logo infringement, a third version was released with a plain white nurse's hat. A fourth, censored version, exclusive to Malaysia, removed Lindemulder's cleavage and edited the semi-nude band shot on the back, but oddly brought back the Red Cross symbol. "Anyway, there were actually four different versions of the cover."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Produced by Tommy Ramone
xref.body: After leaving his drumming role with the Ramones, Tommy Ramone transitioned to a successful career as a producer, notably producing albums for The Replacements. "He also produced albums for the replacements and Red Cross."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tommy Ramone's Death and Later Career
xref.body: After leaving the Ramones, Tommy Ramone co-produced two more of their albums (*Road to Ruin* and *Too Tough to Die*) and produced albums for bands like The Replacements and Red Cross, before forming the bluegrass folk band Uncle Monk. He was diagnosed with bile duct cancer, which spread throughout his body despite treatment, and he died in hospice care on July 11, 2014, at the age of 65. "Tommy was diagnosed with bile duct cancer and spread throughout his body despite treatment. And he died at hospice care on July 11, 2014 at the age of 65."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
